comments.body:
Pushed in 427fcdd960a0867792000d80feb9b10d1f1aa2c0. `results/pilot.json` is the pilot's raw output, unchanged (sha256 9e5fefd1…). It holds 55 trace points of [elapsed_s, samples, estimate], about one every 10 s, from 1e5 to 1.6897e9 samples; the run's final point is 1.7198e9 samples.

`results/pilot_trace.csv` has the same trace plus that final point, the error, and the 95% sampling envelope pi ± 1.96·σ/√n at each n. You can draw the envelope around the pi line, so a reader can see the estimate converging at the expected 1/√n rate. All 55 points lie inside the envelope. These are cumulative estimates from one seed, so the points are strongly correlated: the plot shows one path converging, not independent replicates.

The figure must show pilot claim C1: the running estimate converges to pi, and the final value 3.141550 lies 1.07 standard errors below it, inside its 95% CI.

comments.author: experiment-repo
comments.body:
Partly answered; the pilot's final numbers come in about 8 minutes, so this stays open until then.

Already on main (4bee988):
- `assignment.json` names the delivered paths: `analysis/` and `results/` (experiment-repo: code and numbers), `figures/` (figtab-repo), `report/report.md` (you).
- `results/runs.json`: all three jobs were started together at 2026-10-18T21:18:39Z, unmodified, on local-compute. It gives the job refs, exact commands and nominal durations: pilot about 9 min (540 s of sampling), extended 55 min, extended 120 min. Those are the facts the report needs about the extended runs.
- `analysis/analyze_pilot.py`: the analysis code. The CI method is the script's own Wald interval for a binomial proportion scaled by 4, half-width 1.96·4·sqrt(p(1−p)/n). The code checks this against the raw counts and cross-checks it with a Wilson interval.

The pilot's interim line after about 60 s read 3.141581 from 194,300,000 samples; that is an interim value, not the result.

Still to come: when the pilot ends (about 21:28 UTC) I will push `results/pilot.json` (raw output), `results/pilot_summary.json` (estimate, CI, SE, coverage of pi, z-score) and `results/pilot_trace.csv` (the running-estimate data figtab-repo needs), then reply here and close.

comments.author: experiment-repo
comments.body:
Pushed in 427fcdd960a0867792000d80feb9b10d1f1aa2c0. All numbers are in `results/pilot_summary.json`; please cite them from there.

- Pilot: 1,719,800,000 samples in 540 s, of which 1,350,709,559 fell inside the quarter circle.
- Estimate: pi ≈ 3.141550. 95% CI [3.141473, 3.141628], half-width 7.8e-5, standard error 4.0e-5.
- CI method: the script's own Wald interval, 1.96·4·sqrt(p(1−p)/n). It reproduces exactly from the counts. The Wilson interval agrees to within 4e-9, so the normal approximation is adequate at this n.
- Against the true pi: error −4.23e-5 (relative −1.35e-5), z = −1.07, so the CI covers pi. This is what a correct sampler is expected to give: a deviation of about one standard error.
- Running estimate: all 55 trace points lie inside the 95% envelope pi ± 1.96σ/√n. figtab-repo has the data in `results/pilot_trace.csv` and will draw `figures/` (see figtab-repo#… / experiment-repo#3).
- Extended runs (`results/runs.json`): both started at 2026-10-18T21:18:39Z, together with the pilot. They run 55 and 120 minutes and are still running. Their results are not part of this delivery.
- Analysis code: `analysis/analyze_pilot.py`, with a README. It needs only the Python standard library.
- One caveat worth a sentence in the report: this is a single run with a single seed, so the CI is a sampling interval. The pilot's sample count depends on host CPU speed, because the run is timed rather than sized.

issue.body:
